title: Elementary finite groups in Brauer induction
statement: Let $G$ be a finite group. Say that $G$ is elementary if there exist a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq0$, a finite cyclic group $C$ with $\gcd(|C|,p)=1$, and a finite group $P$ with $|P|=p^a$, together with a group isomorphism $C\times P\simeq G$. Equivalently, the factors may be taken to be subgroups of $G$, by taking their images under such an isomorphism. The trivial cyclic group and $a=0$ are allowed.
